Security and compliance checklist (KMS, SOC2, SSO)
Canary plan for private VPC rollouts

Any objections to short quantized model trial for cost comparison?
Who signs SOW at Nimbus for pilots under $50k?
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Alright everyone, good morning — thanks for joining. We probably have 45ish minutes, quick agenda: status, infra blockers, bench results, and next steps.
[00:12] Rajiv Patel: Morning. Quick heads up, I joined from home — if audio cuts, I'll hop back in. We're green on most creds but still waiting on the KMS OK from our security team.

[00:25] Liam O'Connor: Thanks Rajiv. We saw that in the ticket, Daniel had a couple of follow-ups; we can walk through them now. Also we'll go over the KV cache anomaly from last week's 8k context run.

[00:38] Daniel Kim: Yep, real quick: we need to understand the HSM/KMS integration pattern for private deployment. We can't have keys exported; does Redwood support CMEK with AWS KMS or HSM-backed keys?

[00:52] Maya Chen: Short answer: yes, CMEK supported, and for on-prem we can integrate with customer HSM — there's a small work order though. I'll send the architecture diagram after. It's in the security pack but we can call out the steps.
[01:07] Sofia Martinez: Also, we need the egress IP list for the hosted callbacks. Our VPC firewall team asked for precise CIDRs, can't leave it wide open.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Understood — I'll share the static egress ranges. For the dedicated/private we can do peering so no public egress is required.

[01:30] Ellen Wu: On the model side — ran the sample inference set yesterday. Overall accuracy looks fine but we saw tokenization drift on longer docs, maybe from a different tokenizer preproc. Any ideas?

[01:44] Liam O'Connor: Tokenizer mismatch can happen if the client pipeline uses a slightly different BPE. We can dump token IDs and compare. Also worth checking prompt truncation rules; we had a fallback trim that might have altered prefixes.
[01:59] Rajiv Patel: For the KV cache issue — quick recap: at bursts above ~220 QPS with 8k context we observed a 20-30% increase in tail latency and occasional cache misses.

[02:12] Liam O'Connor: Right — reproduced it in our lab. It seems related to KV segment eviction under concurrent cache repopulation. We're suspecting a race with the sequence alignment for longer contexts when batch consolidation spikes.
[02:27] Sofia Martinez: Is that specific to the quantized variant? We tried both FP16 and 4-bit quant and saw similar tail pain.

[02:36] Liam O'Connor: We saw the effect across quant levels, but it amplified slightly in the lowest-bit modes due to micro-ops reorder. Fixes include slight throttling on continuous batching or increasing the ephemeral cache size.

[02:49] Maya Chen: Operationally, there are three levers: throttled admission, bumping ephemeral cache, or fall back to a compatible model variant (lower context) for very high burst windows. We discussed a canary that ramps traffic and auto-fallback.
[03:02] Ellen Wu: Would fallback mean different embeddings or different generations? We need deterministic behavior for clinical note summarization.

[03:10] Liam O'Connor: Fallback would be to a lower-context model variant with same tokenizer and same prompts; outputs could be slightly different but we can tune prompts to keep deterministic behavior. We'll include regen checks in the rollout plan.
[03:23] Rajiv Patel: Timeline: our compliance review is scheduled 2026-06-24. Ideally we want the VPC canary done a week before that so the security team can validate logs.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Okay, that sets a hard target — canary by 2026-06-17. We'll aim for a dry-run 06-18 per your earlier note; if we need to move it earlier we can try to free up infra.
[03:49] Daniel Kim: For audit logs, is the retention configurable? We need seven years for certain telemetry tied to patient interactions; that's a deal point for us.
[04:00] Priya Rao: Redwood's console supports long-term export to S3/archival; retention windows are configurable via the account settings, and we can add audit export hooks to your SIEM.
[04:12] Sofia Martinez: Great, we'll coordinate with our SIEM folks. Also, can you confirm if traces will include token-level timing or just per-request timings?

[04:22] Liam O'Connor: We capture per-token latency for internal diagnostics, but for customers we expose per-request and optional per-step traces on request. We'll prepare a sanitized example trace for you.
[04:34] Rajiv Patel: On credentials, we handed off the service account but still waiting for the correct IAM role binding for the storage bucket. I put the exact role name in the ticket.
[04:45] Maya Chen: Noted — Rajiv, Thanks. We'll verify after the call and confirm. If it's easier, we can pivot to temporary elevated creds for the canary window.
[04:57] Ellen Wu: Bench numbers — you sent a spreadsheet, Liam. The 95th p99 numbers looked mostly in spec, except that one run on 8k context spiked. Can you walk us through what you measured?

[05:09] Liam O'Connor: Sure — in the lab we ran mixed traffic sim: 70% short-chat, 30% long-doc summarization. At baseline throughput, 95th latency was 220ms for 2k context. For 8k the 95th rose to ~980ms normally, but in burst tests it jumped to ~1.6s with a handful of outliers hitting 2.4s.
[05:29] Sofia Martinez: That 2.4s outlier is the issue; SLO for us is 1.2s 95th, and anything above triggers paging. So we need mitigations before canary.

[05:40] Liam O'Connor: Agreed. Short term we recommend: 1) a small admission throttle for requests that exceed 2k tokens concurrent, 2) ephemeral cache bump in the runtime config, and 3) canary with traffic shaping so we don't hit full bursts during the first 72 hours.
[05:58] Maya Chen: On the billing side — there was a question about quantized model cost delta. We estimated about 35% token-cost reduction at the expense of a slight latency uptick in some profiles.
[06:10] Ellen Wu: Is that 35% across the board or only for gen-heavy workloads? For embeddings we're ok with quantized. For guarantees we need to see A/B on quality.
[06:21] Liam O'Connor: It's workload dependent; generative long-context saves more. We'll run an A/B for a week and provide diff metrics and sample outputs for your evaluators.
[06:33] Rajiv Patel: Security question again — SSO: do you support SAML and OIDC? Our infra team wants SAML for console access.
[06:41] Maya Chen: We support both SAML and OIDC; single-sign-on for the console can be enabled and we can map groups to roles. We'll send the metadata URL and example mapping.
[06:53] Sofia Martinez: For the private deployment — what about network egress cost estimates? Our finance wants to understand approximate incremental network egress on day-to-day traffic.
[07:04] Maya Chen: We don't bill for intra-cloud peering egress in some regions; we'll provide a region-by-region estimate and an example cost calc for your expected traffic profile.
[07:16] Ellen Wu: One more thing — data residency. Some states require that PHI remain in-region. Can Redwood pin models to specific regions and ensure inference occurs inside the region?
[07:27] Liam O'Connor: Yes — routing policy can pin by region and by customer tier. For PII/PHI workloads customers often use Private with VPC-only paths to guarantee residency and isolation.
[07:38] Rajiv Patel: Ok good. Back to actionables: can we confirm the bench you'll run? We need the exact scenarios so we can reproduce it on our side.

[07:46] Liam O'Connor: We'll run three scenarios: baseline synthetic short (<=512 tokens), mixed (70/30 short/long), and long-only (8k). For each we'll do steady state and burst windows (30s bursts). We'll capture per-token latencies, cache hit rates, and memory GC events.
[08:00] Sofia Martinez: Capture network metrics too — retransmits, TCP stalls; last time we saw a correlation.
[08:07] Liam O'Connor: Yep will include. I'll upload the bench run logs and a short runbook on how to trigger the same test from your environment.
[08:15] Rajiv Patel: Regarding the ticket for the KMS — Daniel, any additional asks?

[08:21] Daniel Kim: Clarify if key wrapping occurs on Redwood side or customer side; need a guarantee no plaintext leaves the HSM zone. Also, a key rotation model that doesn't interrupt in-flight tokenization sessions.
[08:34] Maya Chen: We'll include rotation docs; typical pattern is versioned keys with graceful key rollover that preserves in-flight operations — we'll share sequence diagrams.
[08:45] Priya Rao: I'll drop the SOC2 and ISO docs link into the thread now, plus a short checklist that maps your items to our doc sections.

[08:53] Ellen Wu: Great. On the pilot success criteria, quick recap: sub-1.2s 95th for core summarization flows under expected production QPS, reproducible outputs for 95% of test prompts, and no critical security blocker cleared by compliance.
[09:08] Maya Chen: Sounds right. We'll collect a small canonical prompt set and run regression checks; Ellen if you can finalize that doc that'd be awesome.
[09:18] Ellen Wu: I'll do that and share by 2026-06-15.
[09:23] Rajiv Patel: Any procurement/PO timing? If we want dedicated by July we need a PO submitted mid-June.
[09:31] Maya Chen: AE note: we'll share pricing worksheet today; if Nimbus decides to commit to a dedicated baseline we can lock in July capacity. I'll follow up with contract timeline.
[09:41] Sofia Martinez: One last ops note — please include an explicit rollback playbook for the canary: who to call, how to route traffic away, and how long to wait for consistency checks.
[09:52] Liam O'Connor: We'll publish a playbook and run a tabletop with your ops team before the canary.

[10:00] Maya Chen: Okay closing round: restate next steps and owners. Liam will run the enhanced bench and share logs (due 06-14). Maya will send SOC2 + egress CIDRs + pricing (EOD 06-10). Rajiv/Sofia will provide IAM role and CIDRs (due 06-12). Ellen will finalize success criteria (due 06-15). Can we agree?
[10:20] Rajiv Patel: Agreed.
[10:22] Daniel Kim: Agreed.
[10:23] Ellen Wu: Agreed.
[10:25] Maya Chen: Great, thank you everyone. We'll follow up with an email summarizing action items and attach the security packet and the bench runbook. Bye.
[10:30] call ended
